alignments.note: Rule 106: the preverb's 'out' rides inside the compound verb's unit, headed on the verb word; no expressed preposition answers to it.
Infinitival marker is a rule 7 helper on its verb.
Anarthrous noun with supplied indefinite determiner (rule 51).

The Greek is anarthrous here, so no article competes: the supplied generic noun 'raiment' is a rule 7 helper on the substantival adjective and rule 17's generic-noun clause keeps the head on 'soft'. Rule 102 names exactly this anarthrous case as the contrast to the articular one at s011.
Rule 32: substantival article before a participle supplies the pronoun 'they' and nothing else, the ASV writing a second word for the relativizer.

Rule 102: an article whose complement is a substantival adjective takes the nominal the ASV supplies inside its own phrase, so 'raiment' is this article's and the adjective stands bare. Rule 22's article substantivizing with no English determiner is the same case, and rule 17's generic-noun clause does not reach here because a Greek article stands to take the supplied word. The ASV writes no determiner, so the article takes the nominal alone.

The adjective keeps only its own English word, the supplied 'raiment' having gone to the article it stands behind (rule 102). Reading 'soft raiment' whole on the adjective with the article unrepresented remains defensible, but rule 102 records the corpus as unanimous the other way for this shape.
Rule 32: the participle carries the relativizer, headed on 'wear'.
Rule 20: the possessor 'kings'' occupies the English determiner slot, so the article realizes nothing.
Rule 23: the ASV gives 'kings' no determiner.
Genitive noun rendered as the English possessor with 's.

review_notes: Corrected: τὰ μαλακά → 'soft raiment'. The accepted reading left the article unrepresented and gave the whole phrase to the adjective, which is rule 17's anarthrous case. Rule 102 governs an article standing before a substantival adjective: the article takes the supplied nominal and heads on it, the adjective standing bare.

The two 'raiment' words are licensed differently and neither is added: the first by the anarthrous μαλακοῖς as a rule 7 helper, the second by the article τά under rule 102, which rule 103 names in terms as the case where an article rather than a spent noun licenses the repetition.
